subject: general
question: The first Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) of India in 1964 was a Collaborative venture between Atomic Energy of _______ Ltd and NPCIL of India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Canada**__.

__
 
• **The first Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) of India in 1964 was a Collaborative venture between Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd and NPCIL of India**.

 
 
• Plans for building the first Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) were finalized in 1964, and this prototype Rajasthan 1, which had Canada's Douglas Point reactor as a reference unit, was built as a collaborative venture between Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd (AECL) and NPCIL.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **IPHWR-700 (Indian Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor-700) **is an Indian pressurized heavy water reactor designed by Bhabha Atomic Research Center.

 
 
• It is a Generation III reactor developed from earlier CANDU based 220 MW and 540 MW designs.
 
• PHWR technology was introduced to India in the late 1960s with the construction of RAPS-1, a CANDU reactor in Rajasthan.
 
• **All the main components for the first unit were supplied by Canada**__. India did the construction, installation, and commissioning.
 
• In 1974, after India conducted its first nuclear weapons test by Smiling Buddha, Canada ended its support for the project. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **Apsara **is the first nuclear reactor in India.

 
 
• It was built in the year 1956.
 
• It is the first nuclear reactor in Asia.
 
 
 
• **Kamini (Kalpakkam Mini reactor) **is the first fast breeder neutron reactor in India.
 
 
• Uranium-233 is used as the fuel in this reactor.
 
 
 
• **Kudankulam nuclear power plant **is the largest nuclear power station in India.
 
 
• It was established with the collaboration of India and Russia.
